title: Claims about a source are anchored at the point of use, reviews of the owner's writing start from its strongest reading, and public products carry the checks themselves
owner_outcome: Reviews, critiques, attributions, and edits to the owner's publishable text contain no inference presented as a source's content, no unverified category or figure claim, no flag built on a misreading of the owner, and no concession made without checking; and every public-facing AI product carries the applicable checks in its own runtime instructions, because published products do not load this repository.
owner_statement: there are a lot of errors you've exposed here in your reasoning and i'd like to see why and how to prevent that in future with UDA, so collect all the errors
owner_refinement: yes add to UDA, and as usual make sure all public facing projects contain the checks that apply to them since they won't have UDA when published (maybe it requires a refactor)
owner_clarification: ooh my bad, i should have told you which projects are actually public facing... meaning projects that would be apps. how can we avoid this in future? the ones that will be standalone apps are innersignal, askrgior, and possibly pangram-humanization-lab altho i'm nots ure about that yet
owner_clarification_followup: humandesign interviewer GPT is an app that's true
owner_clarification_effect: Public-facing means a standalone app. The declared apps are recorded in portable/PUBLIC-APPS.json: InnerSignal, AskRigor, and the humandesign participant interviewer GPT, with pangram-humanization-lab undecided. The other projects already carry checks through open pull requests; the owner said nothing needs to be undone.

owner_supplied_source.reference: Wu et al., 'Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Key Condition Verification', EMNLP 2024, https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-main.714/
owner_supplied_source.owner_scope: Key-condition verification fits research verdicts (for example, a checker shown only a verdict must name its outcome measure and population). The owner excluded therapeutic companion replies: 'replies from innersignal are natural and not formulaic'.
owner_supplied_source.disposition: Adopted only as a bounded, non-blocking experiment for verdict-style outputs; the paper's test problems were generally short (averaging 52.3 words), with answers that were typically numbers or entities, and its authors name much longer problems as future research.

observed_failure: In a chat review of a published essay and the owner's draft reply to it, the reviewer made 26 errors across four replies. Eleven stated the reviewer's inference as the source's content, including unwillingness where the essay was silent, an outcome the essay left open, 'everyone' in one role when several were not, compressed paraphrases in quotation marks, and, in the rewrite of the owner's reply, a sharpened account of a canonical text and a commentary attribution the commentary did not support. Five resolved the owner's meaning against the owner: a claimed contradiction between a view the owner holds and the owner's warning about its misuse, a misread phrase fact-checked as a prevalence figure, a reductio treated as a misquote, a contested reading stated as a correction, and rejected flags re-raised as warnings about readers. Two were unverified category claims contradicting the owner's stated expertise. Three relied on a secondary figure that its own citation contradicted, the last time in the owner's text. The rest were a verification claimed beyond what was checked, a contradiction across turns, estimates reported as measured durations, a misreported edit, and one concession made without rechecking the source. The owner caught 7 during the conversation. The reviewer's first self-audit logged 15 of the 26 (the owner's 7 and 8 more) and called the owner's draft ready to publish; an independent checker found the other 11, including three in the text the owner was about to publish.
causal_mechanism: Trace facts: the chat surface loaded the owner's saved preferences but not this repository. Those preferences include an anchoring rule scoped to what the owner says about people in the owner's life, a verify-and-cite rule triggered by specific named entities, and clarifying-question rules scoped to complex or emotionally charged situations. No independent check ran until the owner asked for an error audit, and the first audit was done by the same context that wrote the replies. Supported inference: rules triggered by topic did not fire on claims about a text already in the conversation, on claims about what a tradition or field says, or on a review of the owner's own writing; the same context treated a text it had read as a text it had checked, both while writing and while auditing. Not established: whether the reasoning-effort setting contributed. The first self-audit ran after the owner switched the session to the highest setting and still missed 11 errors that an independent checker then found.
normalized_rule: Anchor every sentence about what a source says to a passage at the point of use, including words of scope, frequency, persistence, or consent; label inference as the writer's reading; quote only exact words; search a whole text before an absence claim; recheck a paraphrase when it moves into another artifact and always when it moves into text the owner will publish. Verify category claims and trace figures to their primary source; two figures from one source are one finding. State the scope of every verification and describe one's own edits exactly. Check the source before conceding as well as before defending. Keep claims consistent across turns and report derived quantities at the resolution of their inputs. When reviewing the owner's own writing, flag only what survives the strongest reading, ask when a flag depends on the owner's meaning, report a contradiction only when both statements cannot be true, never re-raise a rejected flag without new evidence, and set no quota. Before delivering a draft that critiques a text, reviews the owner's writing, attributes content to a source, adds facts to the owner's publishable text, or claims verification, run an independent claim check with a claim ledger and a budget. Project the applicable checks into every public-facing AI product's own runtime instructions and record each projection, coverage mapping, and exclusion in the transfer ledger.
enforcement: patterns/reasoning-selection.md carries the category-claim check, figure-provenance check, verification-scope statement, measurement-resolution rule, cross-turn consistency check, and the concession half of the predicate-alignment check.
patterns/whole-argument-reconstruction.md carries the rules for reviewing the owner's own writing.
patterns/editorial-authority-and-lossless-editing.md carries the recheck of facts added to owner-authored text.
patterns/independent-evaluation-separation.md carries the claim check before delivery and the experimental key-condition recoverability probe.

portable/claim-integrity/CHECKS.md is the self-contained pack public products adapt; portable/TRANSFER-LEDGER.json records each project's state; scripts/portable_checks.py validates both and checks project clones for recorded anchors.
evals/review-integrity/claim-anchoring-review-v1.json is a synthetic three-stage regression fixture with an answer key.
tests/test_claim_anchoring_review_integrity.py and tests/test_portable_checks.py require these fragments and files.
transfer_rationale: The failure came from one chat review, but the mechanism is generic: a reviewer that has read a source treats it as checked, rules scoped by topic miss claims made in other settings, and same-context self-review repeats the errors it is meant to catch. Any agent that critiques texts, reviews an owner's writing, or edits text the owner will publish is exposed, and public products that do not load this repository need their own copy of the checks.
limits: Does not ban interpretation; it requires labeling it. Does not make the independent claim check mandatory for drafts outside its trigger. The key-condition probe is experimental and never blocks delivery. The regression fixture is synthetic and cannot prove behavior on real texts. A projected check in a public product is proposed, then merged, then deployed; none of these states implies the next.
scope: Portable review, attribution, and editing behavior for any governed agent, plus projection into public-facing AI products.
